genesis.31.p1.b1.text: “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”

genesis.31.p1.b2.text: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.

genesis.31.p1.b3.text: “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”

genesis.31.p2.b1.text: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,

genesis.31.p2.b2.text: “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.

genesis.31.p2.b3.text: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.

genesis.31.p2.b4.text: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.

genesis.31.p3.b1.text: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.

genesis.31.p3.b3.text: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me.

genesis.31.p3.b4.text: Now get up and leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’”

genesis.31.p4.b1.text: “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?

genesis.31.p4.b2.text: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.

genesis.31.p4.b3.text: So do whatever God has told you.”

genesis.31.p5.b1.text: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels, … to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.

genesis.31.p5.b2.text: Rachel stole her father’s household idols.

genesis.31.p5.b3.text: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, …

genesis.31.p5.b4.text: … crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.

genesis.31.p6.b1.text: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.

genesis.31.p6.b2.text: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

genesis.31.p6.b3.text: “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”

genesis.31.p7.b1.text: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead … and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.

genesis.31.p7.b2.text: “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!

genesis.31.p7.b3.text: I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.

genesis.31.p7.b4.text: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”

genesis.31.p8.b1.text: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live!

genesis.31.p8.b2.text: For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.

genesis.31.p8.b3.text: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing.

genesis.31.p8.b4.text: “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.”

genesis.31.p9.b1.text: “What is my crime?” … “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?

genesis.31.p9.b2.text: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you?

genesis.31.p9.b3.text: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, …

genesis.31.p9.b4.text: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself.

genesis.31.p10.b1.text: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

genesis.31.p10.b2.text: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household—fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks—and you have changed my wages ten times!

genesis.31.p10.b3.text: But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.”

genesis.31.p11.b1.text: “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine!

genesis.31.p11.b2.text: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”

genesis.31.p11.b3.text: “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.

genesis.31.p11.b4.text: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

genesis.31.p12.b1.text: I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.

genesis.31.p12.b2.text: So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

genesis.31.p12.b3.text: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal.

genesis.31.p12.b4.text: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.
